item.title: Emotional farewell for Sigatoka man who died following an alleged assault
item.description: As 38-year-old Vimal Vikash Nand who was allegedly assaulted on Sunday was laid to rest in an emotional ceremony at the Koromumu Cemetery in Sigatoka today, charges are yet to be laid against those who beat him up. Hundreds of people gathered in Kulukulu to pay their last respects to the Sigatoka family today.
item.content:encoded:
As 38-year-old Vimal Vikash Nand who was allegedly assaulted on Sunday was laid to rest in an emotional ceremony at the Koromumu Cemetery in Sigatoka today, charges are yet to be laid against those who beat him up.

Hundreds of people gathered in Kulukulu to pay their last respects to the Sigatoka family today.

While speaking during the funeral service, a close friend of the family said Nand was a kind hearted and a loving man who will always be remembered for his hardworking and kind nature.

He says he was a person of a good character and was very dedicated to his work and family.

He adds Nand was a quite and gentle person who was respectful to others and loved sports.

The close friend says Nand was also a great supporter and a true fan of the Fijian Drua team and the Spain Football team.

It is alleged that Nand and his sons were assaulted on Sunday by the two suspects following a confrontation over an incident involving one of Nand's farm animals.

item.title: Raised with Love, now giving love: Youth pastor Nancy Cakacaka shares her story on fijivillage HerStory at 7 tonight
item.description: Nancy Cakacaka is a senior pastor’s wife, a youth pastor, a mentor and a woman dedicated to shaping the next generation. Lovingly known as Aunty Nancy by many young people in her community, she has devoted much of her life to guiding youths, strengthening their Christian faith and encouraging them to make positive choices.
item.content:encoded:
Nancy Cakacaka is a senior pastor’s wife, a youth pastor, a mentor and a woman dedicated to shaping the next generation.

Lovingly known as Aunty Nancy by many young people in her community, she has devoted much of her life to guiding youths, strengthening their Christian faith and encouraging them to make positive choices.

On this week’s fijivillage HerStory with Temalesi Vono, Nancy opens up about her own journey, from growing up in Bua with her grandparents after her parents separated, to the values of love, faith and discipline that shaped her upbringing.

She also shares her experiences working with young people, the challenges families and youths face today, and her message to young people to listen to their parents, stay grounded in their faith and know that they are loved.

Join us at 7pm tonight for fijivillage HerStory with Temalesi Vono, as we hear Aunty Nancy's story.

item.title: Viseisei pays tribute to late Tui Vuda Ratu Eparama
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/08/2026 Hundreds of people turned up at Viseisei Village in Vuda to pay their last respect to the late Na Momo Levu Na Tui Vuda, Ratu Eparama Kitione Tavaiqia.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/08/2026

Hundreds of people turned up at Viseisei Village in Vuda to pay their last respect to the late Na Momo Levu Na Tui Vuda, Ratu Eparama Kitione Tavaiqia.

Ratu Eparama passed away on July 30th at the age of 95.

T he Thanksgiving Church Service for the late Tui Vuda was officiated by the President of the Methodist Church in Fiji and Rotuma, Reverend Dr. Semisi Turagavou.

The Republic of Fiji Military Forces escorted his casket from the Lautoka Hospital mortuary to his home village of Viseisei yesterday, where his body lay overnight ahead of the burial rites.

Among those attending the funeral are Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprise Manoa Kamikamica; Minister for Justice and Acting Attorney-General Siromi Turaga; Minister for Lands Filimoni Vosarogo; RFMF Commander Ro Jone Kalouniwai; GCC Chair Ratu Viliame Seruvakula; Burebasaga Confederacy High Chief Ro Teimumu Kepa; members of Parliament; members of the diplomatic corps; family; and friends.

In an emotional moment, Ratu Eparama's wife Adi Senitiki Nava Tavaiqia, stood over the casket of her late husband with tears running down her face.

The Commander also paid his respect as the late Tui Vuda was long-serving chief and former military man.

The President and Na Gone Turaga na Tui Cakau, Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu, led a state delegation and members of the Vanua o Cakaudrove to the ireguregu for the late Momo na Tui Vuda yesterday.

He acknowledged Ratu Eparama as a respected and well-regarded leader who will be remembered for his humility, kindness, and service to his people.

Ratu Eparama will be laid to rest today at the traditional chiefly burial grounds in Viseisei Village.

item.description: Commissioner of Police Rusiate Tudravu is standing by a traffic officer for issuing a Traffic Infringement Notice to Opposition Member of Parliament Jone Usamate for illegal parking in the parliament precinct, while Usamate has labelled the actions an overreach on social media. Tudravu says the officer had identified a traffic infringement and acted accordingly, stressing the officer was simply ca
item.content:encoded:
Commissioner of Police Rusiate Tudravu is standing by a traffic officer for issuing a Traffic Infringement Notice to Opposition Member of Parliament Jone Usamate for illegal parking in the parliament precinct, while Usamate has labelled the actions an overreach on social media.

Tudravu says the officer had identified a traffic infringement and acted accordingly, stressing the officer was simply carrying out his duties.

He says Usamate, like any other citizen, has the right to challenge the officer’s decision in a court of law if he wishes to do so.

In a social media post, Usamate questioned the authority of police to issue the ticket within Parliament precinct and called on the Minister responsible for policing and the Commissioner of Police to clarify the matter.

The Commissioner is also urging anyone with complaints about the conduct of police officers to follow the proper reporting channels.

item.title: Predictive AI can never be 100% accurate - David Elbourne
item.description: Predictive AI cannot determine an election outcome with 100 percent accuracy, but clean and accurate data can help provide probabilities that give decision-makers a better understanding of possible outcomes. This follows a presentation by Data Analytics Specialist David Elbourne on the use of AI to predict general elections outcomes at the University of Fiji Press Club, which is led by students st
item.content:encoded:
Predictive AI cannot determine an election outcome with 100 percent accuracy, but clean and accurate data can help provide probabilities that give decision-makers a better understanding of possible outcomes.

This follows a presentation by Data Analytics Specialist David Elbourne on the use of AI to predict general elections outcomes at the University of Fiji Press Club, which is led by students studying Journalism and Media at the University.

Elbourne mentioned this while responding to a question from University of Fiji first-year journalism student Tevita Naturaga on how successful predictive AI has been in developed countries.

Naturaga asked Elbourne about the success of predictive AI overseas, particularly in relation to his presentation on the use of artificial intelligence to predict election outcomes.

Elbourne says predictive modelling has never been 100 percent accurate and referred to his experience in Australia with economic modelling for drought and agriculture, including the impacts of El Niño and La Niña.

He says these models do not provide complete certainty, and the same applies to election modelling.

Insert: Elbourne on AI accuracy 10TH AUG 26

He says predictive modelling is therefore not about guaranteeing who will win an election but using available information to better understand possible outcomes and the uncertainty surrounding them.

Elbourne says the information generated through these models can help decision-makers make informed decisions while understanding that predictions will always carry a level of uncertainty.

Meanwhile Sereina Teilemb, a first-year University of Fiji student , asked what will be the most important role of a human journalist in the future when AI can analyse thousands of documents and predict trends much faster than a journalist.

Fiji Sun representative Inoke Rabonu responded that while AI will continue to evolve and become much faster at analysing information, the role of human journalists will remain important and relevant .

He says regardless of how advanced technology becomes, journalists will still be needed to verify information, ask questions, investigate further and check facts .

Rabonu says the human aspect of journalism will not change , even as AI becomes capable of completing tasks within seconds that previously took much longer.

His key message was that AI may make journalism faster, but it cannot replace the journalist’s responsibility to verify, question and investigate information.

item.title: Turaga unaware of FEO post mistakenly showing fictitious general election date
item.description: Acting Attorney-General Siromi Turaga says he was unaware of the Fijian Elections Office post that mistakenly published a fictitious General Election date yesterday, saying he had not seen the post when questioned about it. Turaga said he did not know and had not seen the post.
item.content:encoded:
Acting Attorney-General Siromi Turaga says he was unaware of the Fijian Elections Office post that mistakenly published a fictitious General Election date yesterday, saying he had not seen the post when questioned about it.

Turaga said he did not know and had not seen the post.

The Fijian Elections Office has clarified that the information was mock content prepared as part of an internal Writ to Return of Writ Dress Rehearsal.

The FEO says the proper procedure for handling the test content was not followed, resulting in it being mistakenly published on its website.

No Writ of Elections has been issued and no date for the general elections has been officially announced.

Under the Constitution, the Prime Minister advises the President on when the Writ of Elections is to be issued.

item.content:encoded:
Two people aged 50 and 48 have been charged by the Fiji Police Anti-Scam Task Force for allegedly obtaining $250 from a victim through an online investment scam advertised on a Facebook account called “Digital Lifestyle”, which promised a $250 return on a $50 investment.

Police say the victim came across the advertisement on Facebook, which claimed that investing $50 would generate a return of $250.

The victim initially transferred $50 and later transferred another $200.

Police allege the money was received and used by the two accused on 20th November 2025.

The two have each been charged with one count of obtaining financial advantage.

They will appear in the Suva Magistrates Court today.
